### Preprocessing

In one paragraph lay out your preprocessing pipeline. No need to provide exact step-by-step detail; just give an overview of the main components:

-   what text content was extracted from HTML

-   how text was cleaned

-   how cleaned text was represented quantitatively

**Multiclass contribution:** The model used cleaned paragraph text from labeled webpages. URLs, email addresses, punctuation, and digits were removed; text was lowercased and whitespace normalized. A TF-IDF vectorizer represented each page using word unigrams and bigrams with sublinear term-frequency scaling. **Binary contribution:** [Team member: add or confirm the preprocessing details for the binary model.]

### Methods

Describe your final predictive models. Include one paragraph with details on the binary classification approach, and one on the multiclass approach. Include for each:

-   what ML/statistical method was used

-   model specification and hyperparameter selection

-   training method

**Binary classification:** [Team member: describe the final binary model, model selection, and training.]

**Multiclass classification:** We compared logistic regression, a linear support vector classifier (SVM), and multinomial Naive Bayes using the same TF-IDF features. On a stratified 80/20 split (1,712 training pages and 428 validation pages; random seed 42), their validation accuracies were 78.5%, 81.3%, and 71.3%, respectively. We selected the linear SVM with class-balanced weights; the vectorizer used a minimum document frequency of one, and the SVM used its default regularization setting. The final model was then fit on all labeled pages.

### Results

Indicate the predictive accuracy of the binary classifications and the multiclass classifications. Provide a table for each, and report sensitivity, specificity, and accuracy.[^1]

**Binary classification:** [Team member: add the binary results table.]

**Multiclass classification:** The selected SVM correctly classified 348 of 428 validation pages (81.3% accuracy; macro-F1 73.8%). The class-specific measures below treat each label as positive and all other labels as negative.

| Class | Validation pages | Sensitivity | Specificity | One-vs-rest accuracy |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| N/A: No relevant content. | 203 | 82.3% | 82.7% | 82.5% |
| Other claim content | 20 | 40.0% | 97.3% | 94.6% |
| Physical Activity | 47 | 59.6% | 97.6% | 93.5% |
| Possible Fatality | 88 | 90.9% | 95.9% | 94.9% |
| Potentially unlawful activity | 70 | 92.9% | 98.0% | 97.2% |

Overall multiclass accuracy is the proportion of pages assigned the correct one of five labels. One-vs-rest accuracy is calculated separately for each class and is distinct from overall multiclass accuracy. “Other claim content” had only 20 validation examples and the lowest sensitivity (40.0%).

[^1]: Read [this article](https://yardstick.tidymodels.org/articles/multiclass.html) on multiclass averaging.
